response.sql: WITH filtered AS (SELECT m.Name AS MediaTypeName, t.UnitPrice AS UnitPrice, CAST(t.Bytes AS REAL) / NULLIF(t.Milliseconds, 0) AS BytesPerMs FROM Track t INNER JOIN MediaType m ON m.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId WHERE t.Bytes > 10323804), per_type AS (SELECT MediaTypeName, AVG(UnitPrice) AS AvgUnitPrice, AVG(BytesPerMs) AS AvgBytesPerMs FROM filtered GROUP BY MediaTypeName), overall AS (SELECT AVG(AvgBytesPerMs) AS AvgOfAvg FROM per_type) SELECT p.MediaTypeName AS name, p.AvgUnitPrice AS avg_unit_price, p.AvgBytesPerMs AS avg_bytes_per_ms, p.AvgBytesPerMs / o.AvgOfAvg AS ratio_to_overall FROM per_type p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE o.AvgOfAvg IS NOT NULL;

assumptions.assumption: The file-size threshold is strict: only tracks with Bytes greater than 10323804 are kept. The request says 'large files' without saying whether the threshold itself counts.
The database is SQLite, so CAST(... AS REAL) avoids integer division and NULLIF(Milliseconds, 0) turns zero-length tracks into missing values that AVG ignores.

Media types are grouped by MediaType.Name, and the across-type average is the plain mean of the per-type averages of Bytes divided by Milliseconds. Rows are suppressed when that overall average is NULL.

alternatives.interpretation: The threshold is inclusive: keep tracks whose Bytes are greater than or equal to 10323804.
